interpretation: Coefficient is skilled/unskilled worker-days per ONE measured unit; crew output per day is min(role_count/role_coefficient), but only when ALL required trades/resources and applicability have been checked. Workdays are not elapsed days; setup/curing/permit waits are separate.

sources.publisher: Government of Nepal, Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation
sources.caveat: Rate-analysis man-day quantities, NOT calendar durations or blanket building productivity guarantees

sources.publisher: Government of Nepal, DUDBC (via Gandaki Province Infrastructure Office)
sources.document: Norms for Rate Analysis of Building Works
sources.caveat: Applicable item, soil class, lead and construction method must be checked in the official PDF before using coefficients

sources.publisher: Nepal Armed Police Force building labour-productivity field study
sources.document: Labor Productivity Assessment of Armed Police Force Nepal Building
sources.caveat: Observed output and quoted DUDBC benchmarks are not signed universal norms; the published study contains an apparent kg/man-hour vs kg/man-day wording error

sources.document: Delhi Analysis of Rates Vol I 2023
sources.caveat: CPWD explicitly says coefficients are indicative, vary with technology/skills/site and are not Nepal-adopted

rates.section: Building norms B1, soft clay/silty soil hand excavation ≤10m lead and ≤1.5m lift
rates.notes: Requires verified soft-soil class and method; manual excavation and spoil stacking as specified; higher difficulty, shoring and water are separate.

rates.section: Building norms B2, compacted earthfill in ~15 cm layers, ≤10m lead
rates.notes: Do not assume 40% recovered soil or that mechanical compactors, shrinkage and material testing are included.

rates.section: Section 7, item 7.1, stones in foundation and levelling, haul ≤30m
rates.notes: Covers stone laying/levelling. Does not separately include user's sand-blinding requirement or acceptance checks.

rates.section: Section 9, mechanically assisted PCC grade M10, 1 m³
rates.notes: User's 1:3:6 PCC must not automatically be assumed grade M10 or equivalent to this mix. Requires spec/engineer confirmation.

rates.section: Section 9, PCC for RCC M20 using mechanical aids, 1 m³
rates.notes: Mixer 0.4h/m³ and vibrator 0.25h/m³ indicated in norm. Placing concrete only; rebar, formwork, curing and inspection separately.

rates.section: Section 7, item 7.3, random rubble masonry with 1:3 cement mortar: per 5 m³, skilled 7 md and unskilled 14 md
rates.notes: Only analogous if project specifies that mortar, wall geometry and access; not suitable for unspecified stone masonry.

rates.section: DUDBC benchmark quoted in building labour study: 0.67 m³ per mason-day; measured sites average 1.41 m³/mason-day
rates.notes: Laboratory/site study context only; helper ratios and 10mm joints with specified brick format not fully identified.

rates.section: Section 13, item 13.1.C, 12.5mm cement:sand 1:4 wall plaster per 100 m², 12 skilled and 16 unskilled md
rates.notes: Application only. Substrate preparation, height access, scaffolding and curing/calendar waiting need separate allowance.

rates.section: Section 13, item 13.5 and 1:4 continuation, 20mm cement:sand plaster per 100 m², 14 skilled and 19 unskilled md
rates.notes: Externally exposed conditions, scaffolds and weather delays are not included in nominal application production.

rates.section: Section 14, item 14.5 A (primer 3+3 md per 100m²) + D (two prepared paint coats 9+5 md per 100m²), additive benchmark
rates.notes: Derived from two separate rate lines: 12 skilled and 8 unskilled md per 100m² total. Excludes surface preparation/drying between coats.

rates.section: Quoted DUDBC benchmark 83.33 kg per skilled worker-day; observed Nepal site sample ~125 kg/worker-day
rates.notes: A secondary quoted benchmark, NOT a full crew production standard: helpers, chair/cover blocks, steel congestion and wastage unavailable.
